A stress-controlled LCF testing method (R = 0.1, frequency = 1 Hz) was established for reduced-thickness specimens at 980 ℃. A total of 15 specimens with 3 surface conditions (bare alloy, MCrAlY coated, and PtAl coated) were tested. The investigation revealed the mechanisms by which oxidation-resistant coatings affect the low-cycle fatigue performance of the single-crystal superalloys. Specifically, the oxidation-resistant coatings were found to reduce the substrate’s fatigue life by up to 80 % under the specified experimental and processing conditions. Premature cracking of the coatings was identified as a key factor contributing to performance degradation. This study provides valuable insights into the fatigue failure mechanisms of coated single-crystal superalloys and underscore the importance of coating integrity under high-temperature cyclic loading.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of oxidation-resistant coatings on the low-cycle fatigue life of reduced-thickness single-crystal superalloy specimens at 980 ℃
metadata.author: Wenqi, Hao;Duoqi, Shi;Hongyu, Qi;Xiaoan, Hu;Xiaojun, Guo;Junyan, Zhu

text: Achieving high recoverability is essential to maintaining the structural integrity for Ni-based superalloy single crystals. However, the recovery and recrystallization mechanisms in Ni-based superalloys after high-temperature deformation are still discussed controversially. This study reveals that for plastic strains of up to 3.2 %, dislocations carry plasticity in superalloy single crystals compressed at high temperatures, and that both dislocations as well as superlattice stacking faults can be easily annealed out by recovery treatment to preempt recrystallization. This means that the recoverability of Ni-based superalloy single crystals can be increased by more than twice compared to previous reports. For larger plastic strains, deformation twins form. They block moving dislocations which assemble in new boundaries that eventually trigger dynamic recrystallization. Upon subsequent heat treatment, such newly recrystallized grains grow rapidly further, resulting in a coarse polycrystalline microstructure. Consequently, avoiding deformation twins becomes the key to maintaining the single-crystalline microstructure.

metadata.source_filename: High-temperature deformation of Ni-based superalloy and recrystallization prevention by recovery
metadata.author: Chen, Kai;Pantleon, Wolfgang;Shen, Hao;Ma, Evan

text: Thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF) is a complex damage mechanism considered to be one of the key issues limiting the service lives of hot section components in a gas turbine engine. Turbine blades and nozzle guide vanes are particularly susceptible to this form of material degradation, which results from the simultaneous cycling of mechanical and thermal loads. In this research, a series of TMF tests were undertaken on a single crystal nickel-based superalloy, CMSX-4 under a variety of phase angles and a thermal cycle of 550–1050 °C, to holistically understand the evolving damage mechanisms that can occur under the various loading conditions. The generated data has shown that for the strain ranges tested, fatigue life is significantly affected by the employed phase angle. Furthermore, the length of time that the material is exposed to elevated temperature has a substantial influence on the material’s microstructure, and thus, the dominant mode of damage that occurs.

metadata.source_filename: The influence of phase angle on the TMF crack initiation behaviour and damage mechanisms of a single-crystal superalloy
metadata.author: Garcia, Alberto Gonzalez;Whittaker, Mark;Lancaster, Robert;Barnard, Nicholas;John, Sean;Doyle, Joseph;Mason-Flucke, Julian

text: This work investigated the interfacial reactions between Ni-based superalloys and SiO2 crucibles during vacuum induction melting. Through thermodynamic and kinetic analyses of the interfacial reactions, the underlying mechanisms of the interactions at the superalloy/SiO2 interface are elucidated. The interfacial reactions are facilitated by elemental diffusion at the interface. The Al atoms in the alloy preferentially diffuse to the interface, where they react with O atoms diffusing from the crucible to form Al2O3. The initially formed Al2O3 serves as heterogeneous nucleation sites for TiC. Consequently, a continuous and uniform Al2O3 layer, along with a discontinuous TiC layer, formed at the superalloy/SiO2 interface. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis confirmed the orientation relationship between the TiC and the superalloy matrix as [01‾1]TiC//[1‾12]γ, indicating that the TiC precipitates from the alloy matrix. A simplified two-factor analysis of variance (ANOVA) of the interfacial reaction layer thickness data reveals that within the temperature range slightly above the melting point of the superalloy, the melting time is the primary factor that significantly affects the thickness of the interfacial reaction layer.

metadata.source_filename: The interfacial reaction process and phase formation mechanism between the nickel-based superalloy and the SiO2 crucible during vacuum induction melting
metadata.author: Wang, Jun;Yang, Haoxue;Liu, Liting;Zhang, Guodong;Cheng, Fasong;Li, Jinshan

text: The creep behavior of CoNi-based superalloys at high temperatures and low stress conditions (960 °C/150 MPa) was investigated. A unique double steady state creep rate is observed as the creep of such superalloy proceeds. The formation of the first steady state creep rate can be attributed to the γ/γ′ interface preventing dislocations from de-shearing the γ′ phase and the formation of <101> superdislocations in the γ′ phase. As a large number of dislocations shear into the γ′ phase, the creep rate increases rapidly. The formation of large size γ′ phase obstructs the other γ′ phase rafting, the superdislocation networks at the interface of large size γ′ phase and a<100> superdislocation in γ′ phase causing a hardening effect, which led the superalloy to second steady state creep rate and improve the creep resistance.

metadata.source_filename: Unique double steady state creep rate and deformation mechanism of a CoNi-based superalloy
metadata.author: Li, Chong;Guo, Qianying;Zhou, Meng;Jing, Ke;Volinsky, Alex A.;Zhang, Yi;Liu, Yongchang

text: In this study, the as-cast Ni-Fe-based superalloy GH4650T (HT650T) subjected to only two steps solution heat treatment shows good mechanical property at high temperature, and the yield strength increases abnormally with the increase of temperature. Correspondingly, the reasons for yield strength anomaly are explored in terms of precipitation behavior of strengthening phases, dislocation movement and evolution trend of grain boundary species. The experimental results indicated that the solution-treated GH4650T alloy can still maintain good mechanical property at high temperature, which is attributed to M23C6 carbides with fine particle morphology distributed along grain boundaries. In addition, the yield strength anomaly observed in solution-treated GH4650T alloy during high-temperature tension is primarily attributed to continuous dynamic recrystallization. Dislocations interact each other through planar slips, forming string-like low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) network inside the grain, the LAGBs network evolves to form sub-grains, and further plastic deformation prompts LAGBs in the sub-grains to transform into high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs). The strong obstruction of HAGBs on dislocation movement eventually leads to the pile-ups of high-density dislocations at HAGBs, which eventually results in the increase of yield strength anomaly of GH4650T alloy.

metadata.source_filename: Yield strength anomaly and microstructural evolution of solution-treated Ni-Fe-based superalloy deformed by high-temperature tension
metadata.author: Ye, Y.J.;Zhang, P.;Yan, J.B.;Liu, P.;Li, L.M.;Zhou, G.Y.;Jiang, H.;Cao, G.H.;Yuan, Y.

text: The selective laser melting (SLM) process for fabricating CM247LC nickel-based superalloy components is often limited by severe cracking. This study explores the use of a post-heating laser track as a method to mitigate cracks during SLM processing by providing localized pre-heating. The effects of post-heating energy input on density, microhardness, cracking characteristics, microstructure, and cracking mechanisms were systematically analyzed. Results show that without post-heating, there was a weak correlation between volumetric energy density (VED) and material density, with densities ranging from 8.18 to 8.60 g/cm3 and peaking at 107.1 J/mm3. Microhardness remained largely unaffected by VED, but a weak positive correlation was observed when post-heating was applied. Cracking characteristics, including crack length and frequency, were significantly influenced by the post-heating energy input, with 80 % energy input yielding the best results in reducing crack lengths. Furthermore, the post-heating process induced grain refinement, increasing grain equiaxity and altering the dominant cracking mechanism from intergranular to ductility dip cracking at lower energy inputs. Although cracks were not entirely eliminated, reducing crack lengths typically offers promising improvements for the fatigue performance of the material. This study highlights the potential of post-heating laser tracks as a practical solution for crack mitigation in SLM-fabricated CM247LC components.

metadata.source_filename: Crack mitigation in selective laser melting of CM247LC superalloy via post-heating laser tracks: Influence on microstructure and cracking behavior
metadata.author: Wu, Aoqi;Li, Siwei;Shi, Lei;Lei, Liming;Shi, Liting;Li, Wenkai;Su, Xuming

text: The tensile behaviors and deformation mechanisms of Co-Al-W-Ti-Ta single-crystal superalloy with different γ' phase size were investigated at 900 °C. As the size of γ' phase (Dγ′) increased, both the Orowan bypassing of γ' by dislocations and the shearing of stacking faults into precipitates were activated simultaneously and competed with each other, which was different from most nickel-based superalloys at high temperatures. However, the density of stacking faults increased first and then decreased since the difference between applied stress and critical stress for shearing into γ' exhibited the same trend. Quantitative analysis of the competitive relationship between these two mechanisms reveals that their competitive relationship governs the variation of yield strength, reaching a peak value of 738 MPa in the specimen with Dγ′ of 320 nm. In addition, under the combined action of yield stress and stacking faults interactions, the ultimate tensile strength has also shown a peak value with the increase of precipitation size.

metadata.source_filename: Dependence of defects competition on tensile behavior in the Co-based single crystal superalloy induced by precipitation size
metadata.author: He, Jinshan;Lin, Ling;Zhang, Runze;Wang, Xitao

text: γ-electrochemical selective dissolution surface modification is a novel strategy for improving K417G nickel-based superalloy machinability. Through γ phase’s dissolution, the K417G nickel-based superalloy’s machining layer can be modified into a porous layer with low strength and hardness, making the machining easier. The modified layer thickness, as a critical factor in determining surface modification’s effectiveness, should be accurately predicted. However, relevant research has not been studied. In this paper, a modified layer thickness prediction model was established for the first time through the combination of theoretical analysis and experimental study. Three key electrochemical parameters, including potential, electrolyte concentration, and polarization time, were considered in the model. The predicted value of modified layer thickness is in good agreement with the experimental value, verifying the feasibility of the model. The model reveals that the potential, electrolyte concentration, and polarization time are positively correlated with the modified layer thickness. The importance of these three electrochemical parameters on modified layer thickness is ordered as: potential > polarization time > electrolyte concentration. This study provides a basis for improving the predictability of γ-electrochemical selective dissolution surface modification technique.

metadata.source_filename: γ-electrochemical selective dissolution surface modification technique for K417G nickel-based superalloy: Prediction model of modified layer thickness
metadata.author: Guo, Xiaoguang;Niu, Lin;Kang, Renke;Dong, Zhigang

text: This study provides a systematic investigation into the size and geometry-dependent microstructural evolution and cracking susceptibility of LPBF-fabricated Rene 41. By coupling experimental microstructural analysis with thermal modeling, this research uniquely identifies the relationship between geometry-specific thermal histories, carbide coarsening, and liquation cracking. Four different geometries with varying thickness were fabricated with the identical process parameters. It was found that the grain size and morphology are not affected by the part size. However, the thinner parts exhibited coarser sub-grain structures compared to the thicker ones. The crack formation was observed for the parts with cross-sections smaller than 1 mm, whereas thicker parts had high density without any defects. The cracks were observed in the interdendritic regions, suggesting that liquation cracking was the active micro-crack formation mechanism. The detailed microstructural analysis combined with a thermal finite element analysis proved that the heat extraction efficiency was lower for thinner parts causing a lower cooling rate and coarser carbides, making them more susceptible to constitutional liquation. Microhardness measurements were conducted for each geometry and correlated with the observed microstructural variations. The findings highlight the critical need for geometry-specific optimization of LPBF process parameters to mitigate cracking and achieve microstructural uniformity, offering valuable insights into the fabrication of complex, high-performance aerospace components.

metadata.source_filename: Geometry and size dependent microstructure and crack formation in Rene 41 superalloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
metadata.author: Sikan, Fatih;Brochu, Mathieu

text: In this study, the tensile behavior of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Ni-based superalloy GH3230 was investigated over a temperature range from low (−195 °C) to high (950 °C) temperatures, elucidating the tensile properties and fracture mechanisms at various temperatures. The experimental results demonstrated that the tensile strength, specifically the yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS), decreased with increasing test temperature. In the temperature range of −195 °C to 20 °C, twinning deformation serves as the main mechanism for plastic deformation. The boundaries of the deformation twins impede dislocation movement, causing substantial strain hardening and resulting in the highest YS and UTS across all tested temperatures. At intermediate temperatures (20–550 °C), dislocation slip becomes the dominant plastic deformation mechanism. Different slip systems were activated during deformation. Above 750 °C, distinct dynamic recrystallization (DRX) was observed within the microstructure, which reduced the strain-hardening effect, alleviated internal stresses, and significantly enhanced ductility. At 950 °C, the bonding strength at the carbide/matrix interface weakened, causing the early formation of voids during plastic deformation, consequently reducing the ductility of the material. This study provides a robust experimental foundation and theoretical basis for predicting and controlling the deformation and failure behavior of Ni-based superalloys at different temperatures.

metadata.source_filename: Temperature dependence tensile deformation behaviors of laser powder bed fusion GH3230 Ni-based superalloy
metadata.author: Liang, Jingyi;Long, Xiaojiang;Zhang, Ning;Chen, Minrui;Tang, Jiafeng;Wang, Ling;Kong, Qungang;Liu, Wenhao;Li, Qingyu;Ren, Ding;Chen, Longqing;Yan, Dapeng;Zhu, Jun;Yin, Ming

text: A new Ni-Co based superalloy with different grain sizes was subjected to creep and interrupted-creep tests at 750 °C/630 MPa. Electron backscatter diffraction and transmission electron microscopy were used to analyze the microstructural evolution and deformation process. The creep results showed that the creep life of the alloy increased by 160 % without lowering the yield strength tested at 750 °C when grain size rose from 26 μm to 59 μm. The fracture characterization results indicated that the failure was mostly caused by stacking fault cutting which improved the creep life, and the density and width of the stacking fault lines were determined by grain size. Compared with the coarse grains, the creep interruption results demonstrated that the stacking faults were more likely to initiate and propagate rapidly in the fine grains at the same strain level. The more grain boundaries and smaller secondary and tertiary γ′ phases in fine grains provided more nucleation sites and made it easier to cut the γ′ phases which also decreased the energy of stacking fault propagation. The formation and failure of stacking faults in the deformation process improved both the strength and creep life for the Ni-Co-based alloy, and this strengthening mechanism can be used to guide the optimization, manufacturing, and application of the alloy.

metadata.source_filename: Effects of grain size on the stacking fault propagation behavior at interrupted-creep process of new Ni-Co based superalloy
metadata.author: An, Teng;Gu, Yu;Du, Jinhui;Dong, Jianxin

text: The cast & wrought process has been widely adopted as the primary forming method for manufacturing superalloy turbine disk components, in which homogenization heat treatment represents a critical procedure for enhancing the hot workability of castings. This study systematically investigates the influence mechanisms of heat treatment temperature on the microstructure and tensile properties of GH4096 nickel-based superalloy ingots fabricated via a novel Electroslag Remelting Continuous Directional Solidification (ESR-CDS) technique. The results demonstrated severe elemental segregation in the as-cast microstructure, with interdendritic regions containing coarse γ′ phases, carbides, γ/γ′ eutectics, and Zr-rich phases. During tensile deformation, cracks were found to preferentially initiate and propagate along these interdendritic zones, leading to low tensile elongation (EL) values. It was revealed that heat treatment temperature critically governs elemental segregation, precipitate characteristics, and mechanical performance: Elevated temperatures progressively alleviate segregation, eliminate γ/γ′ eutectics and Zr-rich phases, and reduce carbide dimensions, while enlarging pore sizes, thereby inducing non-monotonic tensile property variations. Optimal performance was achieved at the heat treatment temperature of 1160°C through substantially reduced segregation, complete elimination of eutectic/Zr-rich phases, minimized carbide sizes (average 3.7 μm) and lowest porosity (0.263 %). Corresponding fracture surfaces exhibited ductile dimple-dominated morphologies, achieving remarkable EL improvements of 101 % (21.1 % RT vs. 10.5 % as-cast; 20.8 % at 700°C vs. 10.1 % as-cast), surpassing other heat treatment temperatures. This work reveals fundamental mechanisms governing temperature-dependent elemental redistribution, precipitate evolution, and deformation behavior, while providing theoretical and technical guidance for optimizing homogenization processes of difficult-to-deform superalloys.

metadata.source_filename: Microstructural evolution and mechanical property response of ESR-CDS processed superalloy ingots to homogenization heat treatment
metadata.author: Sun, Dejian;Zhou, Qiang;Mao, Guo;Li, Xueyang;Yan, Xuewei;Gao, Yang;Fan, Lei;Li, Fulin

text: In this study, a double-seed directional solidification technique was used to produce a series of bicrystal superalloys with two misorientation, i.e., 5° and 20° with different contents of Hf (0–0.4 wt %). The experimental results indicated that Hf addition reduced the size of MC carbides and inhibited the aggregation and growth of M23C6 carbides at both 5° grain boundary (GB) and 20° GB after full heat treatment. As the GB misorientation increased from 5° to 20°, Hf also promoted a morphology transformation of MC carbides from script- and rod-like to blocky, reduced the number of MC carbides and accelerated the precipitation of M3B2 borides. Hf addition significantly improved the transverse creep rupture lives of the alloys with 5° or 20° GB at 980 °C/200 MPa. The effect of Hf on creep properties was more pronounced at higher GB misorientation. It was found that Hf addition optimized the morphology and size of GB precipitates in the as-heat treated alloys, and regulated the coarsening kinetics of these precipitates during creep. This reduced the local stress concentration during creep, thereby increasing the creep rupture lives of the alloys.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of Hf on microstructure and creep properties of nickel-based bicrystal superalloy with different grain boundaries misorientations
metadata.author: Wang, Dong;Zhang, Gong;Shen, Jian;Zhang, Jian

text: The tensile properties of Nimonic 105 alloy after solution treatment at 1150 °C was studied by tensile tests at temperatures between room temperature and 900 °C, and the intermediate temperature embrittlement mechanism of the alloy was investigated through microstructure observation utilizing scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The results revealed that the ultimate tensile strength of the alloy dropped with increasing temperature, while the yield strength remained basically unchanged below 800 °C, above which it reduced sharply. The elongation decreased markedly above 600 °C, and then enhanced gradually with further increasing temperature after reaching a minimum at temperatures of 750–800 °C. TEM examination showed that the primary deformation mechanism was shearing of γ′ precipitates by coupled dislocation pairs below 800 °C, and it changed to Orowan bowing combined with climb and cross-slip of dislocations above this temperature. The ductility minimum of the alloy at 750–800 °C resulted mainly from the precipitation of M23C6 carbides at the grain boundaries and grain boundary segregation of S.

metadata.source_filename: Intermediate temperature embrittlement of a solution treated Nimonic 105 superalloy
metadata.author: Dong, Changfeng;Xie, Dongsheng;Teng, Changqing;Wu, Lu;Yang, Gang

text: Accurately predicting anisotropic damage evolution in crystalline metals remains a challenging topic due to the multiscale nature of fracture. Microstructures play a critical role in influencing crack deflection at the macroscale. To study the relations among anisotropic deformation, crack initiation and propagation, an anisotropic phase-field crystal plasticity model has been developed for nickel-based superalloys. This model differs from conventional approaches in formulating the critical energy release rate as a function of preferentially activated slip or cleavage planes, rather than merely considering it as an isotropic quantity. This development not only allows effective representation of crack initiation due to local anisotropy introduced by slip activation, but also enables a more accurate representation of crystallography-dependent fracture behavior.The performance of proposed method will be demonstrated to characterize crack initiation and propagation in nickel-based single-crystal and polycrystal superalloys. The proposed anisotropic phase field method has been found to be consistent with generalized maximum energy release rate criterion. The findings highlight the significant influence of crystallographic orientation on the crack formation in single crystals. Increased geometrically-necessary dislocation (GND) density has been observed along the activated slip directions, particularly for those near the crack tip. The model capability has also been exhibited in characterizing crack deflection within polycrystalline microstructures. The model is further verified against available experiments reported in recent literatures, by virtue of simultaneously comparing the stress-strain response and crack growth.

metadata.source_filename: Anisotropic phase-field crystal plasticity modelling of fracture in nickel-based superalloy
metadata.author: Pan, Kai;Chen, Yonghui;Zhang, Zhen

text: To achieve a high-strength, high-temperature-resistant joint between silicon nitride (Si3N4) ceramic and GH4169 (55Ni-20Fe-17Cr-5Nb-3Mo), a novel Ti/Au/Ni interlayers was adopted. This strategy was designed to promote the formation of the seam primarily composed of the high-temperature-resistant solid solution. The thermodynamics analysis indicates that the Au-Ni liquid melted the Ti foil and reacted with Si3N4 to form the TiN reaction layer. Meanwhile, the microstructure of the joint was optimized by adjusting the composition ratio of the Au-Ni solid solution (Au-Ni(s,s)). The bonding of Ni foil with GH4169 was achieved through the solid-state diffusion bonding. The typical interfacial microstructure of the bonded joint was Si3N4/TiN/Au-Ni(s,s) + NiTi/Ni(s,s)/Ni foil/Ni(s,s)/GH4169. A two-dimensional finite element simulation model was established based on the actual microstructure of the joint under different bonding parameters. Results showed that the high-level stress concentration within the joint could be ameliorated by the Au-Ni(s,s) effectively. The shear strength reached a maximum value of 131 MPa, bonded at 1100 °C for 90 min, while it was 140 and 60 MPa at high temperatures of 800 °C and 1000 °C, respectively. The work performed furnished the way for the preparation of high-temperature resistant joints from technical and theoretical aspects.

text: Three targets magnetron sputter co-deposition method was adopted to prepare (Nb-Ti)1-x-ySixCry composition spread alloy film. Early hot corrosion behavior of the as-deposited alloy thin film with a mixture of Na2SO4+NaCl salt was investigated at 950 °C for 50 min. Three regions of distinct oxidation behavior can be observed. Region 1 with the composition of Nb-(10–16) Ti-(25–41) Si-(14–20) Cr (at. %) is mainly consisted of SiO2+CrNbO4 and has best oxidation resistance. The reason for that is higher diffusion energy barriers of oxygen in CrNbO4 and SiO2.

text: The investigation evaluated the thermal shock resistance and failure mechanisms of three brazed joints when exposed to 780 °C. During exposure, oxidation of the SiCf/SiC composite leads to the formation of SiO2. Residual oxygen will penetrate the high-entropy alloy while retaining its Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) structure. Additionally, the FCC Cr23C6 phase adjacent to the composite reacted with SiC, producing hexagonal Cr2C, compromising the ability of joint to withstand plastic deformation. Moreover, the presence of Nb (s, s) and significant MoNiSi phases induced a gradual alteration in the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE), facilitating the initiation of shear fractures from the composites towards the central region of the seam, significantly affecting the overall structural integrity and failure behavior of the joint under thermal shock conditions. With an increase in the number of thermal shocks, the shear strength of joint gradually decreases, reaching a maximum of 22.36 MPa after 30 thermal shocks, surpassing that of some joints using glass fillers.

text: Impact response of a solution-treated hot-rolled Inconel 718 superalloy is investigated with plate impact experiments and crystal plasticity finite element modeling. Free surface velocity measurements are conducted along with postmortem microstructure characterizations. The Hugoniot equation of state is determined up to 21 GPa. Dislocation slips, stacking faults and Lomer–Cottrell dislocation locks are predominant deformation mechanisms. A crystal plasticity model considering thermal activation and dislocation drag is developed to simulate shock compression and spallation of the superalloy. This constitutive model reproduces the measured free surface velocity histories. During shock compression, the contributions of 12 independent slip systems to plastic deformation are approximately equal, and plastic strain mainly concentrates at grain boundaries or annealing twin boundaries. There is an increase in the number of active slip systems at higher impact velocities. Simulations reveal both intergranular and intragranular micro-cracks at the primary stage of damage evolution, where intergranular cracks are predominant, consistent with experiments. The present research provides insights into and a useful modeling case for understanding high strain rate deformation and spallation of Inconel 718 superalloy.

text: To provide guidance for the design of high-temperature and long-life wrought superalloys, the microstructure evolution and deformation behavior at high temperature and long-term creep of a novel Ni-Co-based superalloy was investigated. The results showed that the formation of precipitate free zones (PFZ) at grain boundaries (GBs) during long-term creep would facilitate the nucleation of micropores along with the microporous aggregation fracture. Subsequently, the evolution behavior of GBs during the high-temperature and long-term creep was characterized using EBSD, EDS and TEM, revealed the underlying mechanism of PFZ formation. It is mainly attributed to strain-induced GBs migration, which is governed by diffusion. Additionally, dynamic recrystallization (DRX) within PFZs was observed during long-term creep. The DRX mechanism in PFZ is a continuous-DRX with progressive rotation of the crystal lattice. Besides, the secondary γ′ phases within the grain exhibit evidence of rafting, which is closely associated with the deformation mechanism within the grain, primarily attributed to the abundant dislocations surrounding the γ′ phases serving as efficient pathways for elements diffusion.

metadata.source_filename: Creep behavior and microstructure evolution of a novel Ni-Co-based superalloy with long-life designed for high temperature application
metadata.author: Zhang, Rui;Cui, Chuanyong;Zhou, Zijian;Tao, Xipeng;Tan, Yi;Zhou, Yizhou

text: Grain rotation behavior in an IN718 alloy fabricated using laser powder bed fusion and characterized by alternatively arranged large and small grain colonies was examined through exsitu uniaxial tensile testing and electron backscatter diffraction analysis. The results reveal that small grain colonies are mainly located along the centerline of the melt pools and exhibit a higher initial geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density compared with that of large grain colonies. Rotation deformation within grains is heterogeneous, with a broader grain orientation spread as strain increases. Compared with large grains, small grains exhibit more homogeneous deformation. By calculating the rotation angles of 36 grains under various strain ranges, we established correlations between the initial grain orientation, grain size, and rotation behavior. Grain orientation considerably affects rotation behavior, with grains near the [001] corner and [101] corners exhibiting the lowest and highest mean rotation angles, respectively. Additionally, grain size affects rotation as well, with small grains exhibiting greater rotation than large grains. As strain increases, the persistent GND density disparity between large and small grains, along with the restricted rotation of large and irregularly shaped grains, may exacerbate deformation incompatibility, potentially initiating early cracking at the interface.

metadata.source_filename: Grain rotation behavior in an additively manufactured superalloy with alternatively arranged large and small grain colonies distribution

text: This study investigates the γ-γ’ phase structure and dislocation configuration of the nickel-based single-crystal superalloy DD6 subjected to high-temperature, high-speed rotational creep tests at 1050 °C and 20,000 rpm. The centrifugal stress applied through high-speed rotation simulates the actual service conditions experienced by turbine blades in superalloy applications. Creep tests conducted over 200 and 400 h reveal significant microstructural evolution under complex stress states. The results show that the γ-γ’ phase structure evolves differently under the influence of distinct stress components. One stress component induces phase rafting, while another causes the widening of the γ phase, reducing element segregation between the γ and γ’ phases and promoting the precipitation of a secondary γ’ phase. Dislocation evolution is traced from movement within the γ phase to accumulation at the γ-γ’ phase interface, where dislocation networks form and eventually cut into the γ’ phase. The larger centrifugal stress accelerates the evolution of both the γ and γ’ phase structure and dislocation. Additionally, an unusually long and dense dislocation network at the subgrain boundaries is observed, which is believed to result from dislocation pile-up reactions due to misorientation.

metadata.source_filename: Microstructure and dislocation behavior of nickel-based single crystal superalloy DD6 under high-speed rotation and complex stress at 1050 °C
metadata.author: Tan, Yidie;Zhao, Jianjiang;Wang, Fei;Zhang, Ze;Chen, Yunmin;Wei, Hua

text: The present study deals with the site-specific microstructure and porosity evolution, micro-texture and corresponding localized mechanical response of a Nickel-base superalloy (WSU 100) after laser metal deposition (LMD) processing. The as-deposited microstructure contains a sharp heterogeneity in size and geometry of the melt pools as well as development of heterogeneous melt pool microstructure due to the difference in thermal gradient and cooling rate in LMD processing. Identical γ/γ′phase forms irrespective of the location within the specimen although a difference in the crystallite size and residual stresses occur at the bottom region. The as-deposited specimen contains various types of pores (both open and closed) having differences in size and sphericity and are heterogeneously distributed along the build direction. Micro-texture evolution is likewise location specific and varies from a weaker texture near the substrate due to a rapid, multidirectional and complex heating/cooling cycles to a stronger one at the middle region due to the long columnar grains out of the highest temperature gradient and again reverting to a relatively weaker texture near the top surfaces from rapid cooling with no further secondary heating. As a concomitant effect, significant hardness variation on the front surface is related to the local-scale heterogeneities and micro-texture evolution as well as the residual stresses from the LMD processing.

metadata.source_filename: Heterogeneity in site-specific microstructure, porosity, micro-texture and mechanical properties in additive manufacturing of WSU 100 Ni superalloy

text: Developing 9Cr oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) Fe-based superalloy combining elevated-temperature strength and oxidation resistance was a challenge for advanced nuclear applications. A new 9Cr ODS ferrite-martensite superalloy was designed via Al- and Si-alloying, aiming to improve the comprehensive performance at elevated temperatures. The microstructure, mechanical properties and oxidation resistance of 9Cr ODS superalloy were investigated in detail. 1.5Al1Si (1.5 wt% Al and 1 wt% Si) alloy achieved the simultaneous improvement of mechanical properties and oxidation resistance compared with other alloys at elevated temperatures. Multi-scale characterization revealed that the 1.5Al1Si alloy exhibited a refined dual-phase ferritic-martensitic structure (average grain size: 1.47 μm) with coherent Y2Ti2O7 nanoparticles (8.9 ± 2.6 nm), enabling the high tensile strength (648 MPa) at 550 °C. Al and Si co-addition promoted the preferential formation of a continuous Cr2O3 layer after exposure to air at 850 °C for 200 h. Benefiting from the a concrete Cr2O3 protective layer, the oxide scale of 1.5Al1Si alloy did not spall, with the weight gain was only 0.79 mg/cm2. Our work demonstrated that the Al and Si co-alloying was an effective way to improve the comprehensive performance of 9Cr ODS superalloy at elevated temperature.

metadata.source_filename: Simultaneously achieving high mechanical properties and oxidation resistance of 9Cr ODS Fe-based superalloy at elevated temperature via Al and Si-alloying
metadata.author: Li, Jikang;Dong, Shengjie;Liu, Tong

text: The Inconel 738 alloy exhibits high crack sensitivity during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), resulting in poor printability and mechanical properties. Composition modification and powder quality provide an effective method to improve the printability and mechanical properties of Inconel 738 fabricated via LPBF. In this study, the microstructures and properties of a LPBF-built alloy using two types of powders were compared. Inconel 738 alloy powder with a higher B content was prepared via gas atomization, and Mod-Inconel 738 alloy powder with a lower B content was prepared via plasma-rotating electrode powder. The Mod-Inconel 738 exhibited an 87.1 % reduction in defect (cracks and pores) rate (0.002 %) and an 81.1 % reduction in average equivalent defect volume (54.891 μm³) relative to the baseline Inconel 738 alloy constructed via LPBF. Compared with the Inconel 738 alloy prepared via LPBF, the porosity reduction in Mod-Inconel 738 is attributed to the use of a high-quality powder with inherently low porosity, which was produced through the plasma-rotating electrode process. Furthermore, the reduced crack density in the Mod-Inconel 738 alloy manufactured using LPBF was primarily due to the reduced B content. This reduction inhibits the formation of low-melting-point γ+ γ' eutectic phases and borides at grain boundaries, mitigating crack initiation during solidification. In addition, the mechanical anisotropy of the Mod-Inconel 738 alloy produced via LPBF at room temperature was significantly lower than that of the Inconel 738 alloy. Importantly, the elongation of the horizontal sample (Mod-Inconel 738 H) increased by 68.8 % compared with that of the Inconel 738 alloy in the same orientation.

metadata.source_filename: Improving printability of LPBF-built Inconel 738 superalloy via B-modification and high-quality powder
metadata.author: Gao, Yubi;Liu, Bo;Xue, Shengbing;Hu, Yong;Ding, Yutian;Zhang, Dong;Lu, Sujun;Song, Xu

text: A novel Ni-Cr-Fe-base superalloy GH4070T containing around 25 wt% of iron has recently been developed and evaluated as a candidate material of superheater/reheater tubes in the boiler of 700 °C-class advanced ultra-supercritical power plants. In order to determine the optimum addition of iron, the impact of Fe element on the tensile properties and deformation modes of the alloy at 750 °C is investigated by adjusting the Fe content from 15 wt% to around 35 wt%. We found that the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength decrease monotonically with increasing the addition of iron, but the tensile plasticity has an optimum value when the concentration of iron is at 25 wt%. Microstructural observations reveal that the γ′ volume fraction decreases with the Fe content, but without obvious changes in the grain sizes and particle sizes of γ′ precipitates. Meanwhile, it is also found that the primary deformation mode transits from dislocations cutting through γ′ precipitates to dislocations striding over them via Orowan looping and cross-slip/climb with enlarging the concentration of iron, but all the experimental alloys display the mixed-mode fracture. Simulation calculations disclose that the stacking fault energy of the matrix increases with the Fe content, whereas the anti-phase boundary energy of the γ′ phase shows an opposite changing tendency. Given these results, it is deemed that the changes in the microstructural features with the Fe content are responsible for variations in deformation modes and fracture mechanisms as well as tensile properties for GH4070T.

metadata.source_filename: Tailoring the tensile deformation modes in the Ni-Cr-Fe-base superalloy GH4070T at 750 °C by adjusting Fe content
metadata.author: Zhang, P.;Wang, S.;Yuan, Y.;Yan, J.B.;Diao, W.Z.;Huang, L.H.;Nan, Y.L.

text: Material loading test is a necessary approach to characterize the grain deformation and fracture mechanisms. The study of material deformation and failure mechanisms can only be conducted through purposeful deformation and destruction of the materials. However, existing material loading test methods struggle to effectively evaluate deformation states involving severe grain deformation and fracture. In this study, a new material loading test method based on shear-based material removal under the quasi-static condition was proposed. The offset loading configuration between the cutting insert and the specimen induces severe compressive and shear deformation within the deformation zones. Moreover, a microscale quasi-static-cutting (MQSC) test rig was developed to obtain the grain-scale images and microstructure information in the shear-based material removal test (SMRT). Polycrystal Inconel 718 was used as a case study to characterize the severe deformation and fracture behavior of materials. Based on the digital image correlation (DIC) technique and microscopic images taken by the MQSC test rig, the strain and stress fields were obtained to characterize the grain deformation and fracture state at the grain scale. It was found that the fracture mechanisms of Ni-based superalloy can be divided into severe shear-induced fracture and void-crack-induced fracture under severe shear deformation. The SMRT testing method provides a more intense shear and compressive deformation state, offering new insights into the behavior of grains under extreme deformation conditions.

metadata.source_filename: Severe grain deformation and fracture in shear-based material removal test for Ni-based superalloy
metadata.author: Liu, Zhanqiang;Wang, Bing

text: The precipitation behaviors of the strengthening phases (η phase and γ′–γ″ eutectoid microstructure) of the GH4706 superalloy with different solution post-treatment cooling processes are investigated in this study. The precipitation behaviors of the η phase and γ′–γ″ eutectoid microstructure are respectively susceptible to the cooling rates in the ranges of 980–825 ℃ and 825–600 ℃. The η phase exhibits a rod-like and the γ′–γ″ eutectoid microstructure shows a spherical morphology owing to the rapid cooling rate in the range of 980–600 ℃. The η phase grows into a long lamellar shape with a slow cooling rate of 0.5 ℃/min in the range of 980–825 ℃ or during stabilizing treatment at 825 ℃. In order to reduce the interface energy between the lamellar η phase and the matrix, as well as the total energy of grain boundaries, the grain boundaries have to migrate to the matrix without the η phase, forming a cellular morphology with the η phase. Further, the mount of Ti is reduced due to the growth of the lamellar η phase in the cellular microstructure, which restricts the growth of the γ'–γ" eutectoid microstructure. However, the growth rate of the lamellar η phase is decreased with a slow cooling rate of 1 ℃/min in the range of 825–600 ℃, which enlarges the γ'–γ" eutectoid microstructure and facilitates the formation of a cubic morphology through the coordination of strain energy.

metadata.source_filename: Precipitation behaviors of the strengthening phases of the GH4706 superalloy with different solution post-treatment cooling processes
metadata.author: Wang, Lei;Huang, Shuo;Wang, Jiahui;Duan, Ran;Qin, Heyong;Zhang, Beijiang;Zhao, Guangpu

text: A novel electrical pulse multi-stage aging treatment (EMT) method was proposed to ameliorate the microstructure and mechanical properties of GH4099 superalloy fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM). It is noteworthy that the dense nanoscale γ′ phase (with an average particle size of 11.31 nm) rapidly precipitated under a short electropulse duration (66 min). During the EMT process, the Joule heating effect and electromigration collaboratively promoted the diffusion of atoms and reduced the nucleation barrier of γ′ phase. Moreover, the multi-stage aging design avoids coarsening of precipitated phase. The highly dispersed γ′ phase is coherent with the matrix, showing very low lattice misfit and high anti-phase boundary energy, which enhances plasticity. Compared with specimens after common aging treatment (CT), the EMTed specimens obtained a high tensile strength (yield strength of 1069.6 MPa and tensile strength of 1231.1 MPa) and excellent plasticity (elongation of 51.6 %). As a novel heat treatment approach, the EMT method has the advantages of low cost and great efficiency.

metadata.source_filename: Rapid microstructure modification of selective laser melted GH4099 superalloy using electrical pulse multi-stage aging
metadata.author: Ye, Song;Ma, Zongqing;La, Peiqing;Ma, Qian;Miao, Junwei;Qiang, Xiaohu

text: Piezoelectric-film crystal structure, stress, and piezoelectric properties are crucial factors in the proper functioning of high-temperature alloy–steel substrate piezoelectric thin-film sensors. In this work, a high-temperature alloy–steel substrate AlN piezoelectric thin-film sensor was prepared by magnetron sputtering. The effects of annealing treatment on the performance of piezoelectric thin-film sensor and the microstructural changes of the films were analyzed by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectrometry techniques. Results showed a (002) orientation diffraction peak near 2θ= 36.06° after annealing, and the crystal dislocation density decreased with increased annealing temperature. The annealing also effectively reduced the defects during film deposition. Furthermore, the frequency shifts of the E2 Raman peaks at different annealing temperatures showed that annealing 400°C for 30 min was more effective in removing stress from the film, as measured by Raman tests. Meanwhile, test results of the sensor’s piezoelectric coefficient after annealing showed that the piezoelectric coefficient obviously improved. Through multiple tests of the piezoelectric coefficient d33 at 400°C, it can be concluded that the prepared piezoelectric thin-film sensor exhibits good high-temperature stability and excellent repeatability. This work provided an outstanding guide for the preparation of AlN piezoelectric thin-film sensors on high-temperature alloy–steel substrates.

metadata.source_filename: Influence of annealing treatment on stress and piezoelectric properties of high temperature alloy rigid substrate piezoelectric thin film sensors
metadata.author: Guo, Chenguang;Mo, Guowei

text: Powder ball milling was employed as a novel pre-treatment method on the gas atomized powder, its effect on the microstructure, porosity and mechanical performance of the laser directed energy deposition (LDED) of Inconel 718 was studied. The results showed that the base heating and melting penetration of substrate is gradually enlarged with the increase of ball milling intensity, which is mainly attributed to the enhanced scattering laser irradiation to the substrate due to the increased surface roughness of ball-milled powders. Owing to the increased base heating, the formation of Laves phase is dramatically depressed from 17.9 vol% to 7.4 vol% at 200 rpm pre-treatment. Further increasing the ball milling intensity, the molten pool is overheated and the Laves phase formation is reversely increased. Corresponding to the depressed Laves phase formation, the tensile strength is increased from about 830 MPa to 875–877 MPa, and the tensile elongation is increased from about 22 % to 27 %, at an optimal ball milling speed of 200–300 rpm. Porosity formation is also diminished effectively from 0.6–1.14 % to 0.08–0.48 % due to the compaction and collapse of gaseous voids within the hollow feedstock powder during ball milling process. This work demonstrates that powder ball milling is a promising strategy to tailor the microstructure and enhance the mechanical performance of LDED-fabricated Inconel 718 superalloy.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of ball milling on microstructure, porosity and mechanical properties of laser directed energy deposited Inconel 718 superalloy
metadata.author: Liu, Guoxiang;Yin, Shuo;Shu, Da;Guo, Yanbing;Wang, Lyuyuan

text: Element Ta is crucial for the Ni-based single-crystal superalloys (NXs), but its oxidation mechanism remains elusive owing to its complex oxidation behavior. This work reveals that the Ta element was transformed into three Ta-related phases i.e., CrTaO4, Ta-W-Re nanoparticles and Ta2O5. A continuous CrTaO4 interlayer is formed between the CoCr2O4 and Al2O3 layers, which could effectively hinder the oxygen inward diffusion and exhibits a good adhesive property that maintains scale integrity. However, the formation of Ta-W-Re nanoparticles and Ta2O5 phases within the Al2O3 layer significantly alters its structural integrity, transforming the continuous and dense protective layer into a porous and discontinuous morphology, thereby reducing the oxidation resistance of the Al2O3 layer.

metadata.source_filename: Unveiling the oxidation behavior of tantalum in a nickel-based single crystal superalloy through precise microstructural characterizations
metadata.author: Wang, Yang;Wu, Jing;Xie, Pan;Fu, Libo;Yang, Qianjin;Wu, Cuilan

text: This study aims to comprehensively investigate the state of the technological surface layer taking into account the tool wear stage in multi-axis torus milling of a Ni-based superalloy using the author's active cutting edge segment change (ACESC) technique. A mathematical model of the distance between tool paths as a function of the angle of inclination of the tool axis in relation to the active cutting edge segment change technique is established. Addition, a theoretical model of flank wear width is established, taking into account the elastic recovery effect of the material, with an average prediction error of 10 %. Analysis of the surface morphology revealed a scratch with a curved outline, arranged according to the surface velocity vector as a function of the tool rotation angle. This is the result of micro-chipping and adhesion of chips to the cutting edge of the round insert. At the same time, it has been observed that in the boundary zone of adjacent machining marks, adhesion occurs after the elastic recovery of the material. The deformation of the material grains and the distribution of residual stresses depend significantly on the stage of tool wear and the angle of inclination of the tool axis. Based on the results, a new approach for multi-axis torus milling of aircraft engine blades was proposed.

metadata.source_filename: Analysis the surface integrity taking into account the tool wear stage in the multi-axis torus milling of a Ni-based superalloy using the active cutting edge segment change technique and new approach for machining aircraft engine blades
metadata.author: Nowotnik, Andrzej;Mrówka-Nowotnik, Grażyna

text: The IN718 superalloy underwent laser shock peening (LSP) and heat treatment (HT) processes. The electrochemical corrosion behavior of four sample types was evaluated in a 3.5 wt% NaCl water solution. The results indicated that the combined application of LSP and HT (LSP + HT) significantly improved the corrosion resistance of IN718. LSP refined grain size and modified dislocation structure, creating additional diffusion channels and increasing binding energy. These changes promoted the precipitation of higher quantities of γ′ and γ″ phase particles during subsequent HT, accelerating the formation of a protective passivation layer. The HT process concurrently minimized microscopic defects within the crystal structure, significantly enhancing the material's corrosion resistance. Moreover, the corrosion current density of the LSP + HT samples decreased by 76.26 % compared to the as-received (AR) samples. Additionally, surface pitting in the LSP + HT samples was substantially reduced after corrosion, with the average pit diameter decreasing by 53.7 % compared to the AR samples.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of laser shock peening and heat treatment on the electrochemical behavior of IN718 superalloy
metadata.author: Chen, Ruifang;Guan, Zhichen;Qian, Wei;Cai, Jie;Zhang, Deng;Hua, Yinqun

text: The strengthening phases in Ni-based superalloys are the key structures for providing excellent high-temperature mechanical properties, and a current lack of understanding of the very initial step-to-step formation mechanisms for these phases hinders their applications in advanced manufacturing. Here we report the initial formation mechanism of the γ' phase in the GH4099 Ni-based superalloy, which differs from the reported classical and non-classical nucleation theories. Based on the experimental observations, preferable bondings between γ' elements will induce the Al-Al and Ti-Ti clustering, acting as the starting mechanism in the chemical homogeneous superalloy. This spinodal-like chemical modulation causes the uphill diffusion of the γ' elements into the clusters and reduces the energy barrier of the chemical ordering of the γ' phase in them. This transitional initial formation mechanism of the strengthening phase in this alloy will provide a foundamental theory to design the novel superalloys for advanced manufacturing and processing.

metadata.source_filename: Initial γ' phase formation mechanism in a GH4099 precipitation strengthened nickel-based superalloy
metadata.author: Guo, Qianying;Chai, Jun;Chen, Zitao;Li, Jianwei;Dong, Haokai;Ding, Ran;Liu, Chenxi;Ma, Zongqing;Tian, Xuezeng;Chen, Hao;Liu, Yongchang

text: Nickel-based superalloys undergo oxidation in high-temperature corrosive environments, however, the oxidation behavior and mechanisms remain unclear. Combining multi-scale characterization techniques, Molecular Dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT), this study investigated the oxidation behavior of the nickel-based superalloy CMSX-4 during the short-term oxidation in air at 1100 °C, with the aim of revealing the oxidation mechanism. The in-situ weight gain experiment demonstrates that the oxidation of the CMSX-4 alloy perfectly follows parabolic kinetics during the short-term oxidation stage. The sequence of oxidation for alloying elements is revealed to be influenced by diffusion, element concentration, and oxygen partial pressure. Specifically, Ni and Co elements preferentially undergo external oxidation, forming NiO and CoO on the surface of the alloy, while other elements experience internal oxidation. Initially, simple oxides form, and subsequently, some of these oxides react to produce complex spinel phases. Ultimately, a complex four-layer oxide scale develops, comprising an outer NiO and CoO layer, followed by a CoCr2O4 and TiTaO4 layer, then a NiAl2O4 layer, and finally an innermost Al2O3 layer. The presence of a continuous, thick and dense Al2O3 layer ensured excellent oxidation resistance for CMSX-4 superalloys.

metadata.source_filename: Unveiling the short-term oxidation behavior of nickel-base superalloy CMSX-4 in high-temperature air
metadata.author: Xuan, Weidong;Shao, Guanlan;Che, Xueyu;Wang, Shujuan;Qi, Jianbo;Ren, Zhongming

text: Wear-resistant and corrosion-resistant Fe-based high-temperature alloys have great potential in laser additive manufacturing of metallurgical high-temperature friction parts. However, due to the operational temperature range of 400–800 °C, the friction parts of traditional Fe-based high-temperature alloys often exhibit issues such as poor laser formability and unstable high-temperature performance, primarily caused by cladding cracks and porosity defects. This study utilized thermodynamic phase diagram calculations to simulate the hardness and pitting resistance equivalent number (PREN) of Fe-based alloys, optimizing and designing a novel 20CrNiMoBSiY high-temperature alloy with high wear and corrosion resistance. The alloy powders were prepared using vacuum induction gas atomization (VIGA), and the formability, microstructure evolution and performance enhancement mechanism of laser cladded alloy samples were investigated. The results indicate that the optimized composition of the alloy is 20Cr17Ni2Mo2B1.1SiY. The alloy powder has a spherical shape, uniform composition, smooth surface and flowability of 16 s/50 g. The microstructure of the cladded alloy samples primarily comprises M, retained austenite, (Fe,Cr)2(B,C), (Cr,Fe)23(C,B)6, and (Cr,Fe)7(C,B)3. These phases not only exhibit excellent formability but also possess high hardness, corrosion resistance, and superior high-temperature wear resistance. When the laser energy density is optimized to 138 J/mm3, the hardness of the cladding sample reaches 622 HV0.2, the minimum corrosion current density is 5.72 × 10−6 A·cm−2. At 800 °C, the wear rate is 42 % lower than that of the Q235 steel. The mechanism of synergistic enhancement performance of multiphase microstructure evolution in laser cladding alloys was finely clarified. A novel laser cladding 20Cr17Ni2Mo2B1.1SiY high-temperature Fe-based alloy with high wear resistance and corrosion resistance has been obtained. This work provides valuable reference for laser cladding remanufacturing of metallurgical high-temperature friction parts.

metadata.source_filename: The microstructure evolution and performance enhancement mechanism of a novel laser cladding 20CrNiMoBSiY high-temperature alloy with high wear and corrosion resistance
metadata.author: Chen, Jialu;Zhang, Youcai;Cui, Tong;Liang, Jing;Chen, Suiyuan

text: The mechanical properties of γ/γʹ superalloys are governed by the size, shape, and distribution of the γʹ precipitates within the γ matrix. This work explores the feasibility of microstructure tuning by varying cooling rates in a low mass density γ/γ′ Co-30Ni-10Al-2Nb-4Ti-12Cr (at %) superalloy. We observe a strong cooling rate dependence on the morphology, composition, shape, and size distribution of γ′ precipitates. Cooling rates ≥ 6.25 K/s from super-solvus temperature (1413 K) of the alloy show unimodal size distribution of γˈ precipitates with a high number density. Whereas a slower rate of cooling (≤ 6.25 K/s) results in the formation of the bimodal size distribution of γˈ precipitates. For all the cooling rates explored (100, 28, 6.25, 1.625, 0.43, and 0.108 K/s), secondary γˈ precipitates exhibit nearly cuboidal morphology, and power law describes the evolution of their size with different cooling rates. Atomic-scale compositional analysis by an atom probe reveals the composition of secondary γˈ precipitates is dependent on the cooling rates. In addition, we found finer tertiary γˈ precipitates near the secondary γˈ precipitates and matrix interface, while relatively larger tertiary γˈ precipitates away from the secondary γˈ precipitates for the slow cooling rates (1.625 K/s, and 0.108 K/s). This was attributed to the concentration gradient that develops in the γ matrix region in between the secondary γʹ precipitates during continuous cooling. In the light of classical nucleation theory, the results indicate a multi-stage formation of γˈ precipitates whose morphology, size distribution, and composition are found to be dependent on the cooling rates. Hence, these experiments shows the possibility of tuning the microstructure of Co-based superalloys that is critical in governing their mechanical properties.

metadata.source_filename: Influence of cooling rate on the evolution of γˈ precipitates in a low-density CoNi-base γ/γ′ superalloy
metadata.author: Palanisamy, Dhanalakshmi;Pandey, Prafull;Makineni, Surendra Kumar;Mahadevan, Sundararaman;Phanikumar, Gandham

text: The polycrystalline structure of the interdiffusion zone (IDZ) significantly affects the mechanical properties of the PtAl-coated single crystal (SX) superalloys, while its formation mechanism has not been clarified yet. This study systematically investigated the formation of the polycrystalline structure in the IDZ of a PtAl-coated third-generation SX superalloy by analyzing the interdiffusion and microstructural evolution during the coating deposition process, which mainly consists of grit blasting, Pt electroplating, interdiffusion at 900 °C, and aluminizing. The results indicated that the polycrystalline structure in the IDZ was formed during interdiffusion between the Pt plating layer and the SX superalloy, and was determined by the diffusion rather than the grit blasting. Notably, the phase transformation from cuboidal γ/γ’ phases to Pt-rich γ1/γ’1 phases with irregular shapes occurred in the IDZ during interdiffusion at 900 °C, and the phase boundaries and grain boundaries between the IDZ and the SX superalloy coincided. The formation of the polycrystalline IDZ was mainly attributed to the grain boundary (GB) migration induced by the phase transformation, similar to the discontinuous precipitation. Specifically, Pt diffused from the nano-crystalline Pt-plating layer to the SX superalloy mainly along the GBs, inducing the nucleation of Pt-rich γ1/γ’1 phases at the GBs. Subsequently, γ1/γ’1 phases grew in the direction of Pt diffusion, and the GBs migrated along the growth direction of γ1/γ’1 phases concurrently. This study will be helpful for reducing the formation of the polycrystalline structure in the IDZ of the PtAl-coated SX superalloy.

metadata.source_filename: Formation of the polycrystalline structure in the interdiffusion zone of a PtAl-coated third-generation SX superalloy
metadata.author: Li, Yihang;Li, Longfei;Lu, Song;Zheng, Weiwei;Feng, Qiang

text: Superdislocations in Ni3Al precipitates of single crystal (SX) superalloys are activated during ultra-high temperature creep, but such dislocations’ configuration and possible motive mode remains unclear. In this paper, we systemically analysis the microstructure of a model SX superalloy after 116 hours ultra-high temperature stress-rupture test under the condition of 1200 °C / 80 MPa. The γ' precipitates are highly rafted and dense dislocation networks are constructed at the γ/γ' interface after high temperature crept. Using high-tilt transmission electron microscope (TEM), two kinds of superdislocation in the γ' phase with Burgers vector b=[001] and b=[110] are verified to exhibit a 3D non-coplanar configuration. These superdislocations in γ' phase are formed by the combination of two a/2<110> dislocations with different Burgers vectors. The non-coplanarity assumes γ'-dislocation climbing mode has been activated to produce plastic deformation. These results give new understanding of plasticity micro-mechanism of Ni3Al precipitates against ultra-high temperature and helps developing advanced superalloys resisted to elevated temperature.

metadata.source_filename: Superdislocations activated by 1200 °C creep in Ni3Al phase of a single crystal superalloy: Non-coplanar configuration and motion model

metadata.author: Gao, Yuanhang;Zhao, Shiteng;Ru, Yi;Du, Boxuan;Li, Zhuoyang;Yang, Zexu;Gan, Bin;Li, Shan;Zhang, Heng;Liu, Lei;Pei, Yanling;Li, Shusuo;Gong, Shengkai;Xu, Huibin

text: This study systematically investigated the crack formation mechanisms in DZ125 nickel-based superalloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and evaluated the effectiveness of hot isostatic pressing (HIP) in defect elimination, microstructural modification, and mechanical property enhancement. The results revealed that the cracks in LPBF-processed DZ125 alloy are primarily solidification cracks and liquation cracks, whose formation is associated with thermal stress concentration and low-melting-point eutectic phases induced by segregation of Hf/Ti elements. The conduction-mode melt pools (with an aspect ratio ≈0.5) formed at high scanning speeds effectively mitigated crack formation. After HIP treatments at different temperatures (1050°C, 1150°C, and 1230°C), both cracks and pores were significantly reduced, with near-complete densification and almost full recrystallization achieved at 1230°C. Increasing HIP temperature leads to γ′ phase coarsening and columnar-to-equiaxed grain transformation. The 1050°C-HIP samples exhibited enhanced yield strength (859 MPa) due to precipitation of fine γ′ phases (∼100 nm), while the 1150°C and 1230°C-HIP samples show reduced yield strength but significantly improved elongation (17.5% and 21.8%, respectively) owing to γ′ coarsening and recrystallization. This work provides crucial insights for defect control and performance optimization of LPBF-fabricated DZ125 superalloy.

text: This study investigated the effect of Pt-Al coating on the fatigue behavior of a second-generation single-crystal superalloy (DD5) at different temperatures. The Pt-Al bond coat was deposited on the superalloy, and rotating-bend fatigue tests were conducted at 700 ℃ and 900 ℃. The results showed that the bond coat did not affect the fatigue life at 900 ℃ but improved the fatigue strength at 700 ℃ under low-stress amplitude. However, at high-stress amplitude, the bond coat reduced the fatigue performance at 700 ℃. The fracture morphologies and cross-sectional microstructure were characterized to understand the fatigue crack initiation and propagation mechanisms.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of Pt-Al coating on the fatigue behavior of the single-crystal superalloy at different temperatures

text: In this study, the optimization of process parameters and the microstructure evolution of hot isostatically pressed (HIPed) FGH4096 powder metallurgy (PM) superalloy were systematically investigated. For parameter optimization, on the basis of the traditional constitutive equation and thermal working diagram, double-cone compression + heat treatment and inclusion simulation were innovatively added to further optimize the processing parameters. For the evolution of the tissue, the influence of thermal deformation parameters and the recrystallization mechanism were comprehensively studied. In addition, the evolution of PPBs and the γ′ phase, as well as the role of γ′ relative recrystallization, have also been clarified. The optimized parameters are a temperature range of 1070–1100 ℃, a strain rate of 1–10 s−1, and a strain below 1.8. The PPB networks can be effectively broken through high temperature and high strain rate. γ′ phase exhibited dual functionality during thermomechanical processing:Coarse γ′ (~1 μm) promoted DRX and fine γ' (100–300 nm) suppressed DRX. During the hot deformation process of HIPed FGH4096, DDRX is the dominant DRX mechanism, CDRX serves as an auxiliary DRX mechanism, and twins also promote DRX. The findings of this study provide valuable guidance for optimizing the thermal processing of FGH4096, thereby enhancing microstructural uniformity and mechanical performance.

metadata.author: Wang, Jie;Jia, Jian;Tian, Tian;Zhang, Shaoming;Yang, Shufeng;Qu, Jinglong

text: Doping with trace levels of rare earth elements is an effective approach to enhancing the oxidation and hot corrosion resistance of superalloys. In this study, the hot corrosion behaviour of ppm lanthanum (La) (0 ppm, 40 ppm, and 200 ppm) modified CMSX-4 superalloy and the action micro-mechanism of La were systematically clarified and summarised by SEM, EDS, EPMA, FIB and TEM. The results indicated that ppm-level La doping significantly decreased the corrosion rate of the alloy by more than half. However, increasing the doping level of La does not affect the hot corrosion kinetics of the modified alloys. Compared to unmodified alloys, La-modified alloys exhibit a denser and more complete surface corrosion product, resulting in longer weight gain “plateaus” on the weight gain curves. Further analysis shows La segregation provides a short-circuit diffusion channel for oxygen and promotes the external diffusion of Al, Ti, and Ta, thereby improving the integrity and densification of the protective oxide film. The hot corrosion reaction of the alloy with lower La content (40 ppm) is generally more stable.

metadata.author: Li, Jiayu;Song, Yuelin;Jiao, Dian;Zhu, Zhiying;Ma, Xiao;Yuan, Ruihao;Yu, Jianbo;Wang, Jun;Kou, Hongchao;Ren, Zhongming;Li, Jinshan

text: Thermal cycling induces various microstructural changes in superalloys, which differ from those observed under isothermal testing. In particular, creep life under cyclic conditions is considerably diminished compared with isothermal testing. This study investigated the creep behavior of a high-γ′ volume fraction Ni-based single-crystal superalloy at 850°C/500 MPa after thermal cycling from 25°C to 1200°C. This study offers a unique perspective on the intrinsic behaviors of the superalloy. Results revealed that as the number of thermal cycles increases, creep life at 850°C/500 MPa initially increases and then decreases. It was found that the microrafting structure formed by the secondary γ′ phase in the γ channel and the stable dislocation networks contribute to the creep performance of the superalloy. In addition, a relationship is established between the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) and the changes in the size of the γ/γ′ phases. As the number of thermal cycles increased, the microstructural evolution of the alloy was accelerated. The reduction in creep life of the superalloy at 850°C/500 MPa is primarily attributed to two factors: the reduced CRSS required for dislocations to penetrate primary γ′ precipitates and the diminished effectiveness of dislocation network strengthening at γ/γ′ phase boundaries. This study establishes a notable theoretical and experimental foundation for understanding and predicting the creep behavior of superalloys under thermal cycling conditions.

metadata.source_filename: Effects of ultra-high-temperature thermal cycles on the microstructure evolution and creep behavior of a high γ′ volume fraction nickel-based single-crystal superalloy
metadata.author: Kang, Jie;Li, Geng;Zhang, Haobo;Zhong, Zhiyong;Zhang, Heng;Ru, Yi;Li, Shusuo;Gong, Shengkai

text: By adjusting the content of Ta (7 wt.%, 8 wt.%, 9 wt.%) in a Re-free nickel-based single crystal superalloy, creep mechanism of alloys at 980 °C/200 MPa, including damage and deformation, was investigated. The microstructures and dislocation configurations of three alloys were observed at the primary stage, steady-state stage, accelerated stage and creep fracture stage. The results showed that Ta addition significantly increased creep rupture life of alloy, increasing by approximately 1.3 times from 250 h for 7Ta alloy to 570 h for 9Ta alloy. The improvement was primarily attributed to a substantial extension of steady-state duration, which accounted for 26 % to 46 % of the whole creep stage. The creep damage mechanism of three alloys was closely associated with pore cracking, crack propagation, oxidation zone formation, and the precipitation of secondary phase, including granular M23C6 carbides and long needle-like σ phase (a topologically closed packed phase, TCP). Especially, Ta addition markedly accelerated the precipitation of σ phase. Moreover, theoretical calculations aligned well with observations from transmission electron microscopy (TEM) experiments when considering stress threshold for typical deformation mechanisms, confirming that all alloys underwent similar creep deformation mechanism. Dislocations proliferated and moved through gliding-climbing within γ matrix during decelerated stage. Thereafter, stress/strain gradually increased as creep progressed and dislocations began to shear through γ′ phase, ultimately leading to creep rupture. Additionally, the problem of Ta addition enhancing creep rupture life was also discussed in detail from interfacial dislocation network, γ matrix channels width, γ′ rafting thickness and perfection degree. Therefore, Ta addition can effectively facilitate creep properties of the alloy, which served to optimize alloy design and improve long-term reliable service for turbine blades in aero engines and land-based gas turbines.

metadata.source_filename: Insights into the effect of Ta addition on creep properties in a Re-free nickel-based single crystal superalloy
metadata.author: Dong, Jiasheng;Shen, Yingying;Lou, Langhong

text: To address the issue of thermal damage in grinding nickel-based superalloys, this study proposes a synergistic cooling-lubrication process that integrates water-based hybrid nanofluids with a porous self-lubricating internal cooling grinding wheel. This approach aims to achieve efficient, low-damage grinding of Inconel 718. A novel internal cooling wheel structure was designed with computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-optimized flow channels, establishing a 26° offset angle to maximize the velocity of the grinding fluid jet. Performance tests confirmed that the prepared water-based graphene oxide/multi-walled carbon nanotubes (GO/MWCNTs) hybrid nanofluids exhibit excellent thermal conductivity and stable shear-thickening rheology. Additionally, porous self-lubricating abrasive rings fabricated from polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and nickel-coated molybdenum disulfide (Ni-coated MoS₂) solid lubricant facilitate rapid nanofluid penetration on the wheel surface without compromising mechanical properties. Experiments conducted on a nanofluid-porous wheel internal cooling grinding platform demonstrated that the new process reduced the grinding zone temperature by 34.2%, decreased surface roughness by 65.9%, increased residual compressive stress, and eliminated subsurface damage compared to conventional methods. This improvement is attributed to the nanofluids' ability to rapidly deposit nanoparticles during wheel infiltration, forming a shear-thickening lubricating film in the grinding zone, which enhances cooling and lubrication efficiency. This method effectively addresses thermo-mechanical coupling challenges, providing a high-performance machining strategy for aerospace alloys.

metadata.source_filename: Synergistic Nanofluids-Porous self-lubricating Internal Cooling Wheel for Superalloy Grinding
metadata.author: Peng, Ruitao;Gao, Jiangxiong;Li, Yibo;Tang, Xinzi;Chen, Xiang;Tan, Ziyuan

text: This study presents a comparative investigation on the hot corrosion behavior of Mo-rich single-crystal superalloys with simple aluminide coatings and Co-modified aluminide coatings under molten salt corrosion by 75 wt. % Na2SO4 + 25 wt. % NaVO3 mixture at 750°C and 900°C. The results reveal that Co doping significantly enhances the resistance of aluminide coatings to combined sulfur-vanadium hot corrosion at both low and high temperatures. During hot corrosion, the Co-modified coating develops a multilayered oxide structure consisting of CoO/CoAl2O4/Al2O3. This unique microstructure formation can be attributed to the synergistic effects of Co-induced suppression of outward Al diffusion in the coating and the dissolution of the outer Al2O3 scale by VO3- ions. Furthermore, the presence of CoO effectively reduces the inward penetration tendency of VO3-. At the elevated temperature of 900°C, Co addition demonstrates additional benefits by inhibiting the outward diffusion of Mo from the substrate, promoting its solid solution stabilization in the interdiffusion zone. This mechanism effectively suppresses MoO3 dissolution into the molten salt, thereby preventing acidification-induced acceleration of hot corrosion propagation.

metadata.source_filename: Effect of Co doping on hot corrosion behavior of aluminide coating on Mo-rich single-crystal superalloy exposed to Na2SO4+NaVO3 at 750°C and 900°C

text: The effects of single and double step aging heat treatments were studied for the Nickel-Based superalloy UNS N09925. Single step aging heat treatment at a temperature range from 600°C to 760°C resulted in uniform grain size microstructure coupled with fine M23C6 carbides uniformly distributed on an austenitic matrix, without the formation of continuous networks of secondary phases in the grain boundaries. However, the corresponding result for yield strength of the material in this condition was lower than the values typically achieved by the alloy. Increasing the aging temperature to a range of 800°C and 850°C resulted in precipitation of deleterious phases such as sigma and eta, as well as an increase on M23C6 carbide formation in the grain boundaries. On the other hand, aging the alloy for a longer period of time at 720°C slightly improved the hardness and yield strength, but it also resulted in an undesirable carbide precipitation showing continuous networks of these secondary phases on the grain boundaries, which could cause sensitization and be detrimental to the material properties. Finally, performing a double step aging heat treatment considerably improved the mechanical properties of the material, mainly due to the higher volume fraction of the γ′ precipitate, and neither continuous networks of carbides nor the formation of deleterious phases such as sigma and eta was observed.

metadata.source_filename: STUDY OF SINGLE STEP AND DOUBLE STEP AGING HEAT TREATMENT ON A NICKEL-IRON-CHROMIUM SUPERALLOY
